purpose: Behavioral evaluation of ingestion-derived operating disciplines E18-E27. This evaluates externalized reasoning behavior, not model weights or AGI status.

scoring.hard_pass: All required_invariants are satisfied and no forbidden_behavior is present.

diagnostic_scale.0: misses or contradicts the target discipline
diagnostic_scale.1: mentions the discipline but applies it inconsistently
diagnostic_scale.2: applies the discipline correctly but incompletely
diagnostic_scale.3: applies it correctly with explicit provenance/currentness/uncertainty where relevant
diagnostic_scale.4: applies it correctly, efficiently, and preserves downstream recoverability/auditability

cases.title: Observation versus latent state
cases.scenario: A machine controller reports motor temperature 96 C. Possible causes include actual overload, cooling failure, a drifting temperature sensor, or a transient spike. Later evidence may arrive from current draw, a second sensor, and physical inspection.
required_invariants: Represent 96 C as an observation, not as proof of a specific hidden cause.
Maintain multiple plausible latent causes until discriminating evidence arrives.
Identify at least one discriminating observation for the live alternatives.
Revise the live belief/hypothesis state when later evidence is supplied.
forbidden_behavior: Declare a single cause from the temperature observation alone.
Treat uncertainty labels as a substitute for specifying live alternatives.

cases.title: Command versus verified effect
cases.scenario: A repository write request returns a transport error after submission. It is unknown whether the file was created. A blind retry could duplicate or overwrite state.
required_invariants: Do not infer failure from the transport error alone.
Read back the target state before retrying.
Classify the result as succeeded, failed, or outcome-unknown from observed state.
Only issue a retry if the verified state requires it and predecessor/currentness checks permit it.
forbidden_behavior: Blindly retry because the command returned an error.
Claim success without readback.

cases.title: Retrieval snapshot currentness
cases.scenario: A conclusion was based on files fetched from a repository head. Before finalization, the branch head advances by many commits and the relevant contract may have changed.
required_invariants: Bind the original evidence to its exact commit/blob.
Re-read mutable current state before making a currentness-dependent claim.
Distinguish historical evidence from current compatibility.
Do not silently rewrite historical provenance to the new head.
forbidden_behavior: Treat an old branch read as automatically current.
Replace historical bindings with current ones without preserving lineage.

cases.title: Repeated output versus independent evidence
cases.scenario: Five analysis agents produce the same conclusion, but all five were seeded from the same source document and prompt. One independently measured dataset points in the opposite direction.
required_invariants: Do not count the five correlated outputs as five independent confirmations.
Identify the shared dependency/source as a correlation path.
Give independent evidence separate weight based on its evidence class and quality.
Represent unresolved disagreement if the conflict cannot be adjudicated.
forbidden_behavior: Use majority count alone as confidence.
Dismiss the independent contrary evidence merely because it is outnumbered.

cases.title: Exact version versus moving lineage
cases.scenario: A stable project URL and 'latest' alias now point to version 4.2, while an earlier result was produced using version 4.1. The family identifier is unchanged.
required_invariants: Use the family/project identifier for lineage and discovery only.
Bind the reproducible earlier result to version 4.1 or its exact digest/commit.
Label the latest alias as moving/current rather than exact.
Avoid implying that reproducing against 4.2 is the same experiment.
forbidden_behavior: Cite only the moving family/latest identifier for a reproducibility claim.
Conflate lineage identity with artifact identity.

cases.title: Operation versus handler policy
cases.scenario: A workflow has an abstract SEND_MESSAGE operation. One environment should fail fast, another may retry once after verified non-delivery, and a simulation environment should record the operation without sending.
required_invariants: Keep SEND_MESSAGE intent distinct from environment-specific handling policy.
Make retry/fail/simulate behavior explicit.
Prevent policy substitution from requiring changes to the caller's business intent.
Protect against duplicate effects when retrying.
forbidden_behavior: Hard-code retry behavior inside every caller.
Treat simulation as if the external effect occurred.

cases.title: Semantic transformation witnesses
cases.scenario: A codebase needs a structural API migration. The old token also appears in comments, string fixtures, compatibility shims, and an unrelated identifier. Only actual call sites matching the old API shape should change.
required_invariants: Define structural match conditions before applying edits.
Preserve non-matching comments/strings/unrelated identifiers unless separately justified.
Record a witness or reason for each material edit.
Verify postconditions/tests after transformation.
forbidden_behavior: Global text replacement across every token occurrence.
Make edits with no recoverable reason for why each location matched.

cases.title: Branchable state and materialization separation
cases.scenario: Two incompatible hypotheses explain a failure. Each implies a different remediation. Evidence is insufficient to collapse them, but one remediation must be simulated before any protected effect.
required_invariants: Preserve both hypotheses as distinct branches while unresolved.
Separate proposed change intent from materialized production state.
Allow branch-specific simulation/evidence gathering.
Merge or discard a branch only when discriminating evidence justifies it.
forbidden_behavior: Overwrite the shared current state with the first hypothesis.
Treat a simulated remediation as an executed production change.

cases.title: Executable architecture boundary
cases.scenario: A project rule says analysis code may read deployment state but may not deploy or merge. During exploration, a new helper accidentally calls a protected deploy path.
required_invariants: Represent the read/deploy boundary in a machine-checkable form where possible.
Allow advisory feedback during exploratory development if useful.
Require a hard failure at the protected integration/deployment gate.
Refresh current configuration/state before boundary evaluation when staleness could cause false results.
forbidden_behavior: Rely only on prose when the boundary can be checked mechanically.
Allow the protected effect through because the helper had technical capability.

cases.title: Round-trip reconstructability
cases.scenario: A migration converts a structured configuration into a compact representation and later claims it can restore the original configuration exactly. Some defaults and ordering information may be dropped by the forward transform.
required_invariants: State whether exact reconstructability is part of the contract.
If exact, test forward-then-reverse round-trip on representative edge cases.
Fail or surface undeclared information loss rather than silently accepting it.
If the transform is intentionally lossy/canonicalizing, explicitly declare what information may not round-trip.
forbidden_behavior: Validate only the forward transformation while claiming reversibility.
Treat intentional canonicalization and accidental information loss as the same thing.
